at room temperature (RT), the aging precipitates effectively hindered the movement of basal dislocations, and the activation of non-basal dislocations is rather difficult, resulting in the alloy's high strength and low plasticity.
When the precipitate is introduced by aging treatment, the yield and tensile strength of the T6 samples are enhanced while the elongation has no obvious change.

These results suggest that the LPSO–precipitate structure still exerts a remarkable strengthening effect at 200 ◦C.

As the temperature further increased to 250 ◦C, dislocations could cut through the aging precipitate particles, and the interior of the grains could provide partial deformation. Hence, the tensile elongation of the alloy was significantly enhanced, increasing from 4% to 12% as the temperature was elevated from 200 ◦C to 250 ◦C.
When the temperature reaches 250 ◦C, the plasticity of the alloy is improved but its strength decreases.
